en.title: Adverbs of manner
en.summary: Adverbs of manner tell how an action is done.

paragraphs: Adverbs of manner tell how an action is done. They answer the question how? and usually modify a verb. They are often formed from adjectives. Choosing the right adverb makes a description exact: walk slowly, speak clearly, work hard.

Many adverbs of manner are made by adding -ly to an adjective. Some have the same form as the adjective, such as fast, hard and late, and the adverb of good is well. Adjectives ending in -y change to -ily, and adjectives ending in -le drop e and add y.

Use an adjective to describe a noun and an adverb to describe a verb. She is a careful driver, but She drives carefully. After verbs such as be, look, feel and seem, we use an adjective: She looks happy.
Some adverbs have two forms with different meanings. Hard means with effort, but hardly means almost not: He works hard, He hardly works. Late means not on time, but lately means recently.

items: Wrong: **She sings beautiful.** Right: **She sings beautifully.**
Wrong: **He plays good.** Right: **He plays well.**
Wrong: **I feel happily.** Right: **I feel happy.**

ro.title: Adverbe de mod
ro.summary: Adverbele de mod arată cum se face o acțiune și au adesea aceeași formă ca adjectivele masculine la singular.

paragraphs: Adverbul de mod arată cum se petrece o acțiune. Acest cuvânt răspunde la întrebarea „cum?”. Adverbul determină de obicei un verb și nu își schimbă forma după gen sau număr.

În limba română, multe adverbe de mod au aceeași formă cu adjectivul la masculin singular. De exemplu, spunem „băiat frumos” și „el cântă frumos”. Există și adverbe cu formă proprie, cum este „bine” pentru adjectivul „bun”. Spre deosebire de adjectiv, adverbul nu se acordă cu substantivul.
